name: Test Sufficiency
checks: Core high-risk paths have tests: auth/permission, billing/payment/webhook, data consistency/idempotency
Unit tests isolate external dependencies; integration tests exercise real boundaries with controlled environments and explicit prerequisites.
Mock external I/O in unit tests when appropriate; do not replace the real boundary in a test whose purpose is integration, persistence or read-back.
Test names communicate behavior and condition in the project’s test-runner convention.
Pure logic / domain layer tests have minimal or no mocks
Mocks are placed at module boundaries only, not on internal implementation details
Tests assert contracts (input/output), NOT internal implementation steps
Failure / unhappy / edge paths are tested (not just happy path)
State transition correctness is tested (for stateful features)
Validation/schema has negative tests (invalid input rejected)
Test failures are locatable and reproducible — when a test fails, the failure message and test structure make it possible to identify the exact cause without re-running in debug mode
Cleanup/rollback behavior is tested — features that create resources, open connections, or write state have tests verifying proper cleanup on success and rollback on failure

Thread-through invariants use positive end-state assertions — when Plan invariant says "X threads through Y to downstream Z", tests assert `downstream.X == expected` (end-state equality), NOT signature inspection (`inspect.signature` / `typeof` / reflection); signature-only tests pass but cannot catch dead param (see UNIT_TEST_GENERATION_GUIDELINE §7B Thread-Through Positive-Assertion Rule)
PR has automated test feedback — CI runs tests on PR and results are visible before merge [SHOULD]

Test file names reflect module/contract, not phase/cycle artifacts — no `test_worker_phase15.py`-style names; rename via git mv at first commit opportunity (see UNIT_TEST_GENERATION_GUIDELINE §20.1) [SHOULD]
No low-cohesion test files (test_helpers/test_misc/test_infrastructure) — each test file maps to one concern (see UNIT_TEST_GENERATION_GUIDELINE §20.2) [SHOULD]
Superseded tests removed in same commit as replacement — no stale passing tests shadowing newer stronger coverage (see UNIT_TEST_GENERATION_GUIDELINE §20.3) [SHOULD]
Shared fixtures placed in scope-aware shared location (conftest.py/BaseTest/beforeAll/TestMain), not duplicated per-directory (see UNIT_TEST_GENERATION_GUIDELINE §20.4) [SHOULD]

checks.check: Every reachable decision branch introduced by the change has a test, and loop boundaries cover zero, one and many.

Test generation considers all eight scenario classes: happy path, validation failure, authorization failure, dependency failure, retry/duplicate/replay, state transition, cleanup/rollback, and empty/boundary/malformed input.
Per-layer test focus and mock rule for each of the seven layers (config, domain, orchestration, execution units, adapters, projections, entry surfaces).
Long-lived processes are tested beyond the happy path: claim/lock, cleanup and artifact lifecycle, state transitions asserted on real state, checkpoint recovery, concurrency guard, failure handling.
Adapter tests cover request payload shape, response mapping, and error interpretation with retry.
Config tests cover missing required config crashing at startup, invalid format producing a clear error, and coercion.
UI components are tested across props, loading, empty and error states.
When a new test is genuinely stronger and covers the same invariant, the old one is deleted in the same commit.
Integration tests are few and aimed at the high-risk seams; external systems get contract tests or stubs.
A thread-through that changes a signature also enumerates callers and justifies the ones not threaded, so no dead caller path goes untested.

anti_patterns: Over-mocking until tests lose meaning (mock everything, assert nothing real)
Tests generated without reading architecture or source context
Asserting implementation details instead of contract behavior
Projection tests that accidentally verify projection as truth

Treating prompt template as more important than test design — test quality degraded because focus is on crafting the "perfect prompt" for AI-generated tests rather than designing meaningful test scenarios and assertions

Signature-inspection tests for thread-through invariants — `assert 'kwarg_name' in inspect.signature(f).parameters` passes trivially, doesn't catch dead kwarg; downstream never receives value despite "signature accepts" → P1 runtime bug

Migration text-grep — schema migration verified via `str_contains`/`grep` on SQL text instead of schema introspection (`information_schema`/`pg_catalog`/`sqlite_master`/`SHOW CREATE TABLE`); brittle to whitespace/casing/ordering changes (E4) [P2 should-fix]

Source-grep negative-presence — runtime behavior asserted by grepping source text (e.g. `grep "deprecated_field"`) instead of runtime behavior verification, AST walk, or pre-commit lint hook; passes when text is renamed but behavior survives (E5) [P2 should-fix]

Duplicate count-tripwire sites — same count invariant (e.g. "tool count = N") hardcoded in multiple test files; every addition/removal requires multi-file edits and risks partial update; should have single canonical assertion site with shared constant (E6) [P3 note]

Worker happy-path-only coverage — worker/daemon/scheduler has tests only for normal execution success, with no tests for claim/lock, cleanup/artifact lifecycle, checkpoint recovery, concurrency guard, or external write safety; flag as coverage gap even if all existing tests pass (E9) [P2 should-fix]

Test caller pattern fidelity gap — test setup 引入 production caller 不存在之 synthetic outer wrap（context manager / fixture stack / DI scope），測得 synthetic-mode behaviour 而非 production behaviour；對比 production caller invocation 上下文與 test setup → flag P1（per UNIT_TEST_GENERATION_GUIDELINE §10A）
why: Review guidance, not an enforced checker or proof of review completion. Apply each question to this repo’s actual scope and architecture; state when it does not apply. Source names and R-/PL- identifiers are historical attribution, not required files in the adopter. Historical measurements below describe the recorded experiment, not a new measurement.
